summary: Gradual 5xx drift and elevated error-rate during mixed embedding + chat burst (connection throttle amplification)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ScribeAI started seeing a steady increase in 5xx responses (502/503/504 mix) across both embedding and chat routes during a multi-tenant burst window. The increase was gradual: error-rate climbed from baseline ~0.2% to ~6% over ~45 minutes, then partially recovered after tenant-fairness shedding.

Impact:
- ScribeAI reported 20% of requests receiving 5xx errors at peak for ~30 minutes; visible in their dashboard and invoices under the dedicated pool.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/embeddings/batch.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east (dedicated pool for ScribeAI, mixed workloads).
- Autoscaler configured with burst capacity and priority-shed policy.
- Runtime version: rwd-runtime v2.14.1.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Replay customer traffic: mixed small-embedding batches (~64 items) + short chat streaming requests with keepalive.
2. Simulate concurrency ramp from 50 tps -> 220 tps for 10 minutes then steady at 180 tps for 30 minutes.
3. Observe accept-queue, prefetch lock contention and increased API gateway 502s.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returning 502/503 with downstream upstream reset messages.
- Runtime processes intermittently restarted with OOM-like logs and NVML driver warnings (non-fatal resets).
- k-v cache eviction rates spiked, prefetch latencies grew 5-10x.
- Connection throttle counters increased on the proxy layer leading to hedged-retry amplification.

Expected behavior:
- Priority shed should gracefully limit low-priority embeddings without cascading upstream resets or runtime restarts.

Initial hypothesis:
- Mixed workload caused accept-queue backpressure, prefetch lock thrashing, and connection-throttle feedback that pushed runtimes into GC/driver-thaw cycles, producing gradual 5xx drift rather than a single crash event.

Attachments / logs:
- Api-gateway traces: trace ids provided to customer on request.
- Runtime logs: nvml warnings, mem-alloc failbacks, kvcache eviction logs (see investigator notes).
- Grafana links: latency & error-rate dashboards attached in related_confluence_pages.

investigation_notes:
- Observed pattern: accept-queue depth and api-gateway conn-throttle counters rose before runtime warnings. Hedged retry policy amplified concurrent retries, which increased prefetch pressure and caused kvcache hot-shard evictions.
- Runtime logs indicate memory fragmentation and transient NVML warnings consistent with frequent driver resets on noisy GPU nodes. No single deterministic OOM crash found; rather many small allocation failures and GC thrash.
- Correlated with scheduler logs showing backoff loops triggered for prefetch workers, exacerbating request queuing.
- Hypothesis validated in controlled replay: disabling hedged retries or reducing embedding concurrency prevents the 5xx gradient.
- Related config: priority-shed window of 30s was too short for this mixed workload.
resolution:
Mitigation performed: lowered embedding priority and enabled a transient prefetch backoff (applied at 2026-03-10 12:00 UTC) which immediately reduced 5xx rate.
Follow-up permanent actions planned:
1) Admission-control update to smooth connection-throttle hysteresis and reduce hedged-retry amplification (PR planned, runtime Eng owner: Liang Chen).
2) Prefetch worker backoff + per-shard token limit increase to avoid hot-shard eviction loops.
3) Autoscaler threshold adjustments to provision burst capacity earlier for mixed embed/chat patterns.
4) Runbook update: guidance for dedicated customers on submitting mixed high-frequency embedding + streaming traffic and SDK throttling patterns.
Target timeline: canary for admission-control changes in 72 hours, full rollout in 1 week after validation.
actions_taken: 1) Temporary priority change for ScribeAI embeddings (done 2026-03-10 12:00 UTC). 2) Load replay and tracing captured; artifacts uploaded to Confluence and linked. 3) Engineering PR created for admission-control hysteresis: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1723. 4) Customer advised to stagger embedding uploads or enable client-side rate limiting until rollout completes.
